To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the computer simulated rocking curves from the model presented in this paper, are in better agreement with experimentally measured curves than the curves from the other two models.
the Takagi-Taupon-Abeles model provides a good description of the experimental rocking curves for the InGaAs/GasAs SLSs.
the dynamic approach is superior to both the kinematic and the dynamic approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computer code to calculate the X-ray diffraction rocking curve from a superlattice.
the development of an efficient method to simulate rocking curve profiles of superlattice samples.
the development of a method to simulate the X-ray double crystal rocking curves for superlattice structures using the Abeles-Takagi method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Abeles-Takagi model is the best approach for the simulation of X-ray diffraction rocking curve of superlattices and that the Takagi-Taupon method alone is not sufficient for the simulation of superlattice rocking curves.
the Takagi-Taupon and Abeles matrix model gives the most accurate results for the calculation of X-ray diffraction rocking curves of superlattice samples.
the Takagi-Taupon method is the best approach in simulating the rocking curves for the SLS structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the case of a SLS on a substrate, the Takagi-Taupon model is the best for the case of small superlattice period, the Abeles-Takagi method is best for medium period and the kinematic approach is the best for large superlattice period.
the dynamic model is more accurate than the other models.
the Takagi-Taipin approach gives better results for SLS with a small number of periods and the Abeles-Takagi model gives better results for the superlattices with a large number of periods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Takagi-Taipin method is the most appropriate for the simulation of the rocking curve of a SLS structure.
the Abeles-Takagi (AT) approach is a more robust and versatile method for simulating the dynamic X-ray rocking curves of superlattice samples.
the dynamic Takagi-Abeles approach is more suitable for the analysis of the experimental rocking curves of SLS structures.
